title: First Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Escazú Agreement: Rules of Procedure, Election of Officers, Committee Structure, Financial Arrangements, and Human Rights Defenders in Environmental Matters
executive_summary: The First Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Escazú Agreement (April 2022) adopted key decisions including the Rules of Procedure, election of Presiding Officers, and establishment of a Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance. The Committee, composed of seven independent members, will promote implementation, review compliance, and ensure public participation. Financial arrangements were agreed upon, establishing a Voluntary Fund managed by the Secretariat. The Conference set dates for future meetings, including an extraordinary meeting in April 2023 to elect Committee members and a second ordinary meeting in April 2024. An open-ended ad hoc working group on human rights defenders in environmental matters was created to prepare an action plan and hold annual forums, emphasizing protection and support for environmental human rights defenders. The meeting underscored transparency, public participation, gender balance, and geographical representation in all processes, aiming to strengthen environmental governance and access rights in Latin America and the Caribbean.
characteristics: The Escazú Agreement establishes a Conference of the Parties (COP) with rules of procedure adopted at its first meeting, including public participation modalities and meeting logistics.
The COP meets at least biennially, with provisions for extraordinary meetings, and is chaired by elected Presiding Officers serving staggered terms with geographic and gender balance.

A Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance is established as a subsidiary body, composed of seven independent members with expertise, tasked with promoting implementation, reviewing compliance, and engaging public participation.
Decision-making prioritizes consensus, with voting procedures defined for substantive and procedural matters, including secret ballots for elections.
Public participation is significant, allowing attendance, statements, document access, and involvement in subsidiary bodies, facilitated by a regional public mechanism.
Financial arrangements include a Voluntary Fund managed by the Secretariat under UN rules, with calls for stable, predictable funding to support implementation.

Political Actors: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States

practical_applications: Adoption and implementation of the Rules of Procedure of the Conference of the Parties to the Escazú Agreement, including modalities for significant public participation in meetings.
Establishment and election of Presiding Officers (Chair and Vice-Chairs) to lead the Conference of the Parties, including one elected public representative with voice but no vote.
Creation of the Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance as a subsidiary body to promote and support implementation of the Agreement, with adopted rules on its structure and functions.
Procedures for nomination, election, and terms of Committee members, ensuring equitable geographical distribution, gender parity, and legal expertise.
Mechanisms for the Committee to receive, register, and consider communications alleging non-compliance, including protection measures for public members filing communications.
Provision for significant public participation in the Committee’s functions, including rights to provide information, participate in meetings, and engage in dialogues.
Establishment of a Voluntary Fund as a UN trust fund to finance implementation activities, administered by the Secretariat with transparent financial reporting.
Secretariat functions carried out by the Executive Secretary of ECLAC, including meeting organization, document circulation, and financial management.

Scheduling of ordinary meetings of the Conference of the Parties at least every two years, with extraordinary meetings as needed, including a planned extraordinary meeting in Argentina in April 2023 and a second ordinary meeting in April 2024.

Establishment of an open-ended ad hoc working group on human rights defenders in environmental matters to prepare an action plan, hold annual forums, and promote national measures to protect these defenders.
commitments: The Presiding Officers elected at the first ordinary meeting shall remain in office until the closure of the second ordinary meeting of the Conference of the Parties, including any extraordinary meetings in the interim.
The public is requested to designate one of its elected representatives to the Presiding Officers within two months of the adoption of the decision I/2.

Members of the Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance shall serve a term of four years, renewable for another four years. Of the members elected at the first election, three shall serve a term of six years determined by lot.
The Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance shall hold in-person meetings at least once a year.
The Committee may not receive communications on the compliance of a Party before the closure of the second meeting of the Conference of the Parties.
The Committee may not receive communications on a Party’s compliance until one year after the entry into force of the Agreement for that Party.
The Voluntary Fund to support the implementation of the Agreement shall be administered as a trust fund under UN regulations, with no earmarking of contributions.
The Secretariat is requested to continue exploring additional sources of funding to support activities planned for the 2022–2024 period.
The Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean is requested to allocate additional resources from its regular budget to support the Agreement.
The Conference of the Parties agrees to consider financial arrangements at its second ordinary meeting.

An extraordinary meeting of the Conference of the Parties shall be convened tentatively on 20 and 21 April 2023 in Argentina to elect inaugural members of the Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance and consider other matters.
The second ordinary meeting of the Conference of the Parties is tentatively scheduled for 22 to 24 April 2024.

The open-ended ad hoc working group on human rights defenders in environmental matters shall prepare an action plan to be presented at the second ordinary meeting of the Conference of the Parties for consideration and adoption.
An annual forum on human rights defenders in environmental matters shall be held, with a final report prepared to serve as input for drafting and review of the relevant action plan.

kpi_list.kpi_text: Ordinary meetings of the Conference of the Parties shall be held at least once every two years, unless the Parties decide otherwise.
kpi_list.target_description: Hold ordinary meetings at least once every two years
kpi_list.measurement_method: Counting number of ordinary meetings held per two-year period

kpi_list.kpi_text: Extraordinary meetings of the Conference of the Parties shall be held as decided by the Conference at an ordinary meeting, or at the written request of any Party, provided that at least half of the Parties have expressed their support within 90 days of the request being communicated to the Parties by the Secretariat.
kpi_list.target_description: At least half of the Parties must support the request for an extraordinary meeting within 90 days
kpi_list.measurement_method: Verification of support percentage and timing of responses
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Conference of the Parties and Secretariat

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Presiding Officers shall meet every six months preferably in a virtual format or when circumstances warrant.
kpi_list.target_description: Hold at least two meetings of Presiding Officers per year
kpi_list.measurement_method: Counting number of Presiding Officers meetings held annually

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance shall be composed of seven members, serving in their personal capacity.
kpi_list.target_description: Maintain a Committee composed of seven members

kpi_list.kpi_text: The term of office of Committee members shall be four years, renewable for another four years.
kpi_list.target_description: Committee members serve four-year terms, renewable once
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking term durations of Committee members
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Committee shall hold in-person meetings at least once a year and virtual meetings with the frequency defined in its working modalities.
kpi_list.target_description: Hold at least one in-person meeting annually
kpi_list.measurement_method: Counting number of in-person meetings held per year
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Committee shall provide a systemic report periodically submitted by the Committee to the Conference of the Parties on implementation of and compliance with the Agreement. The Committee shall decide on the periodicity of its systemic report in its working modalities.
kpi_list.target_description: Produce and submit systemic reports on implementation and compliance periodically as decided by the Committee
kpi_list.measurement_method: Submission and review of systemic reports by the Conference of the Parties
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Secretariat shall submit, at each meeting of the Conference of the Parties, a consolidated report on the finances and implementation of the activities financed by the Fund, prepared in accordance with the financial regulations and accounting and reporting procedures of the United Nations.
kpi_list.target_description: Submit consolidated financial and implementation reports at each Conference of the Parties meeting
kpi_list.timeframe: at each Conference of the Parties meeting

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Conference of the Parties agrees to convene an extraordinary meeting, to be held in Argentina, tentatively on 20 and 21 April 2023, in order to elect the inaugural members of the Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance and consider any other matter decided by the Parties.

top_actors.name: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
top_actors.justification: This actor is central as the Escazú Agreement is a regional treaty specifically for Latin America and the Caribbean. The Conference of the Parties, composed of these States, is the main decision-making body throughout the document, adopting rules, electing officers, and guiding implementation.

top_actors.name: Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC)
top_actors.justification: ECLAC acts as the Secretariat for the Agreement, providing administrative, logistical, and financial support. It is repeatedly referenced as the body responsible for secretariat functions, hosting meetings, and managing the Voluntary Fund, making it a key institutional actor.

top_actors.name: Governments
top_actors.justification: Individual governments of the Parties are the primary actors implementing the Agreement, represented by delegations at meetings, electing Presiding Officers, and responsible for compliance. Their role is fundamental in decision-making and operationalizing the Agreement's provisions.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism
top_themes.justification: The document is fundamentally about the first meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Escazú Agreement, a regional multilateral environmental treaty. It extensively covers procedural rules, decision-making, institutional arrangements, and cooperation mechanisms among Parties, highlighting the centrality of multilateralism in achieving the Agreement's objectives.

top_themes.name: Digital Governance
top_themes.justification: While not explicitly focused on digital governance, the document includes references to digital modalities such as virtual meetings, electronic communications, paperless documentation, and webcasting of sessions. These elements reflect the integration of digital governance tools to facilitate transparency, participation, and efficient administration.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: The document emphasizes meaningful public participation, including provisions for vulnerable groups and indigenous peoples, and the use of virtual platforms to ensure broad access. This reflects a commitment to digital inclusion as a means to enhance transparency, equity, and social development within the governance framework.
